## LorebookEntry

Type definitions and JSDoc typedefs for the inksprite application.

## Type Files

- **models** - Data model type definitions (Story, Part, Scene, etc.)
- **composables** - Composable return types and interfaces

## Type System

inksprite uses JSDoc annotations for type safety without TypeScript:

- All functions have explicit parameter and return types
- Complex types are defined as JSDoc typedefs
- Type checking is done via `npm run typecheck`

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** The story's id
- `lastDocumentId` **([string][111] | null)?** The document the writer is in: the editor's

- `openDocumentIds` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** The documents open in the editor, in tab
  order. Absent means one tab, the last document; see `utils/tabs.js`.
- `previewDocumentId` **([string][111] | null)?** The open document that is only being
  looked at, whose tab the next one opened from the outline takes. Absent or

- `layout` **[StoryLayout][14]?** How the writer left the panels. Absent means the
  default arrangement; see `components/writer/layout/layout.js`.
- `version` **[number][112]** Bumped each time it is saved

## TtsVoice

A voice a project is read in: a name for the writer, and what the speech
server is asked for.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** voice_xxx, or `narrator` for the default
- `name` **[string][111]** What the writer calls it: Narrator, Riley
- `voice` **[string][111]** What the server is asked for, as written. A Kokoro mix

## SpeakerAssignment

One block given to one voice: a paragraph, or a stretch of speech in one,
or what stands around it. Remembered by the block's text and where it was,
so it can be found again after the document changes.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `text` **[string][111]** The block as spoken, one space between words
- `index` **[number][112]** Where it was among the blocks when assigned
- `voiceId` **[string][111]**&#x20;

## StoryNarration

How a project is read aloud. All of it optional: a project that has never
been read has none of this and reads in the default voice.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `voices` **[Array][114]<[TtsVoice][22]>?** Absent or empty means the one default voice
- `defaultVoiceId` **[string][111]?** The voice for blocks given no speaker. Absent,
  or naming a voice since removed, means the first.
- `narratorId` **[string][111]?** Legacy. What `defaultVoiceId` was called for its

- `providerId` **[string][111]?** The connection it is read aloud through, which its

- `model` **([string][111] | null)?** The connection's model it is read aloud with

## Document

A node in a story's document tree. Replaces Part and Scene: a folder is what
a Part was, a text document is what a Scene was. Both keep their original
ids, so anything already pointing at a `part_xxx` or `scene_xxx` still
resolves.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** doc_xxx, or a migrated part_xxx / scene_xxx / drafts_storyId
- `storyId` **[string][111]** Owning story
- `parentId` **[string][111]** Parent document id, or the storyId when at the root
- `order` **[number][112]** Display order among siblings
- `type` **(`"folder"` | `"text"` | `"file"`)** Folders hold children, text holds
  content, and a file is something imported — a PDF, an image — whose bytes
  are kept beside it (see `stores/filesStore.js`) and whose `content` is the
  text that could be read out of it.
- `mime` **[string][111]?** Files only: the media type, `application/pdf`,
  `image/png`. What decides how it is shown and whether a model can be
  handed it.
- `size` **[number][112]?** Files only: the file's size in bytes
- `pages` **[number][112]?** Files only, and only for a format that has
  pages: how many
- `ordered` **[boolean][113]?** Folders only. Ordered folders sort by `order` and
  accept drag-to-position. Unordered folders sort by title. Absent counts as
  unordered.
- `handOrder` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Folders only, while sorted by name after
  being kept in order: the ids in the order the writer had, taken up again
  when the folder is kept in order once more.
- `kind` **[string][111]?** What this document is, when it came from somewhere
  with a shape of its own: `card` on the folder an imported character card
  became, the field's name on each of its documents, `lore` on a book. Read by
  the importer and the exporter and nothing else — the titles belong to the
  writer, so a renamed document is still found by this. Absent on an ordinary
  document, which is most of them.
- `source` **[RepositorySource][34]?** Repository folders only
  (`kind: 'repository'`): where the code under it was read from, which a
  refresh reads again. See `source/`.
- `drive` **[DriveLink][36]?** Text documents only: the Google Doc it was
  imported from. Absent on any other document, and on a copy of one.
- `edited` **[number][112]?** Roots only: when something in the project last
  changed, a document in it or a message in one of its chats, to the minute.
  What the project picker shows. Absent on a root written before it was kept,
  until the picker works it out.
- `hidden` **[boolean][113]?** Kept from the model. A hidden document is left out
  of the project the AI is shown and out of reach of its tools, and so is
  everything under a hidden folder. Absent counts as shown.
- `title` **[string][111]** Document title
- `convertedFrom` **[string][111]?** For a Markdown copy a conversion wrote, the
  document it was converted from; a later conversion of that one replaces it
- `plain` **[boolean][113]?** Edited as plain text and stored as typed, never
  settled to what the editor can show. For prompts and the like. Absent counts
  as a structured document.
- `content` **[string][111]** Markdown; always empty for folders. For a file,
  the text extracted from it at import, a PDF's page by page under `[p.N]`
  markers — what the model reads and searches, and what a scan has none of.
  Stored as typed, like a plain document.
- `speakers` **[Array][114]<[SpeakerAssignment][24]>?** Who speaks which block when the
  document is read aloud. An overlay on the blocks, found again by their text
  when the document changes; see `tts/script.js`. Absent means the default voice
  reads all of it.
- `summary` **[string][111]** Document summary
- `wordCount` **[number][112]** Word count; always 0 for folders
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## RepositorySource

Where a repository's code came from: a GitHub repository at a ref, or a

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `from` **(`"github"` | `"folder"`)**&#x20;
- `name` **[string][111]** `owner/repo` for GitHub, the folder's name otherwise
- `ref` **[string][111]?** The branch, tag or commit asked for; absent for

## DriveLink

The Google Doc a text document came from. Kept so that syncing the two, when
it comes, can reach the Doc again without the writer picking it a second
time; nothing reads it yet. See `.llm/google_docs_design.md`, part 3.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** The Doc's file id in Drive

## StoredFile

The bytes behind a file document, in a table of their own so that loading

### Properties

- `blob` **[Blob][115]** The file, carrying its media type

## Chat

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique chat identifier (chat_xxx)
- `storyId` **[string][111]** Parent story ID
- `title` **[string][111]** Chat title
- `titleSet` **[boolean][113]** Whether title has been set (auto or manual)
- `lastMessageAt` **([number][112] | null)** Timestamp of last message
- `description` **[string][111]?** Chat description/purpose
- `messageCount` **[number][112]?** Number of messages in chat
- `profileId` **([string][111] | null)?** Chat profile this chat runs on, built-in or the writer's own. Absent, or naming one since deleted, means the profile its project starts chats on.
- `promptId` **([string][111] | null)?** Legacy. The library prompt this chat ran on before prompts became profiles; kept as the record of what it was pointed at. See `stores/migrations/profiles.js`.
- `disabledTools` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Names of tools withheld from this chat. Absent means every registered tool is offered.
- `disabledToolGroups` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Group ids withheld from this chat, which also withholds tools added to those groups later.
- `mcpServers` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** The MCP servers whose tools this chat is offered, by id, once the writer has chosen here. Absent means the servers that list the chat's profile. A server's tools are opted into rather than withheld, so a server connected later reaches no chat that did not ask for it. See mcp/servers.js.
- `web` **[boolean][113]?** Whether this chat searches the web, once the writer has chosen here. Absent means it does when web search is set up for the chat's profile. Opted into, as a server's tools are. See web/config.js.
- `voiceId` **([string][111] | null)?** The voice this chat's messages are read aloud in, one of the project's. Absent, or naming a voice since removed, means the project's default.
- `prompt` **[string][111]?** The chat's own system prompt, once the writer has changed it here. Absent means the profile's, read on every turn. See ai/profiles.
- `rules` **[string][111]?** The chat's author's note: standing instructions the writer keeps as they go, sent in their latest message after the project block and ahead of what they said. Starts as the profile's. Absent means none.
- `pinnedIds` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Documents whose text rides in the project block from the first turn, without the model having read them. A folder pins what is under it. Absent means none.
- `shownIds` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Documents this chat sees although a folder above them is hidden in it: a character's own folder, under the folder all the characters are in. Absent means none.
- `hiddenIds` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** Documents kept from this chat's model, and everything under them unless something nearer is pinned or shown. The document's own `hidden` keeps it from every chat. See `utils/visibility.js`. Absent means none.
- `userVoiceId` **([string][111] | null)?** The voice this chat's own messages are read aloud in, one of the project's. Absent means the same voice everything else is read in.
- `userName` **[string][111]?** The writer's name in this chat: what `{{user}}` becomes in what its model reads. Asked for when a chat on a card starts. Absent means the macro is read as written. See `cards/macros.js`.
- `characterName` **[string][111]?** The name of the character this chat plays: what `{{char}}` becomes in what its model reads. Absent means the macro is read as written.
- `roleplayPrompt` **[string][111]?** Roleplay instructions sent after the system prompt, or where it says `{{original}}`: a card's system prompt, for a chat on a card. Kept apart from the prompt so that saving the chat to its profile does not take the card with it. Absent means none. See `withOriginal` in cards/card.js.
- `postHistory` **[string][111]?** Roleplay instructions sent after the author's note, or where they say `{{original}}`: a card's post-history instructions, for a chat on a card. Absent means none.
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

- `type` **`"function"`** Call type (always 'function')
- `function` **[Object][110]** Function call details

## ReasoningDetail

Reasoning detail entry from OpenRouter extended thinking

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `type` **[string][111]** Type of reasoning (e.g., 'reasoning.text')
- `text` **[string][111]?** Reasoning text content
- `signature` **[string][111]?** Cryptographic signature for continuation
- `format` **[string][111]?** Format identifier (e.g., 'anthropic-claude-v1')
- `index` **[number][112]** Index in the reasoning chain

## ApiMessage

API message format. One entry per actual model invocation or tool result
within an assistant turn. Assistant entries carry only the text streamed
during that iteration (delta, not cumulative).

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `role` **(`"assistant"` | `"tool"`)** Message role
- `content` **([string][111] | null)** Message content (delta for that iteration)
- `tool_calls` **[Array][114]<[ToolCall][42]>?** Tool calls (for assistant messages requesting tools)
- `tool_call_id` **[string][111]?** Tool call ID this is responding to (for tool result messages)
- `reasoning_details` **[Array][114]<[ReasoningDetail][44]>?** Reasoning blocks (intra-turn continuation only; stripped on replay)
- `_document` **[string][111]?** The document a read put in front of the model. Ours, not the API's, like `_path` and `_hash`: stripped before the message is sent. See ai/context/reads.js.
- `_path` **[string][111]?** The path the document was read at
- `_hash` **[string][111]?** A hash of the text the read saw, for telling whether the document has changed since
- `_reasoning` **[string][111]?** What the model thought during this iteration. Ours, not the API's: the service renames it to whatever the backend calls the field, or drops it. Intra-turn only, so it is never stored on a trajectory.
- `_consultation` **Consultation?** On a skill's result: what the skill did on its way to the answer, for the turn to show. Ours, not the API's: stripped before the message is sent, like `_document`.
- `_dropped` **`true`?** On a `use_skill` result: the writer dropped what it loaded, so it is not carried past a summary. Sent back where it is until then. See ai/skills/loads.js.

## ConsultedCall

What a skill did on its way to its answer, kept beside the answer for the
writer to read.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `thinking` **[string][111]?** What it thought, when the model thinks
- `calls` **[Array][114]<[ConsultedCall][48]>** The tools it called, in order
- `reply` **[boolean][113]?** It wrote the turn's reply, which is the
  message's content. Its thinking is then the message's too, after the
  turn's own, so it is not kept here as well.
- `name` **[string][111]** The tool
- `arguments` **[string][111]** What it was asked, as the model wrote it
- `result` **[string][111]** What it answered, cut short when long
- `consultation` **Consultation?** When the tool was itself a skill: what that one did

## TurnUsage

Token usage for one assistant turn, which may span several requests when
tools are called.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `promptTokens` **[number][112]** Context size of the turn's final request
- `completionTokens` **[number][112]** Generated tokens, summed over requests
- `requests` **[number][112]** Model invocations in the turn

## ChatCommand

A tool the writer ran themselves, from the chat, with no inference involved.

`input` and `param` are kept as typed rather than as parsed, because
rerunning has to ask the same question, and because they are what the writer
is given back when they edit one. `label` and `result` are what the model is
shown; `detail` is the working — the likelihood a question was asked at, the
dice behind a total — and stays in front of the writer, who chose it.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `name` **[string][111]** The command that was run
- `input` **[string][111]** Everything the writer typed after the name, verbatim
- `param` **[string][111]?** What was in the parentheses, for the commands that take something there
- `character` **`true`?** Set when this is somebody speaking rather than something answering. See ai/commands.js.
- `prompt` **`true`?** Set when this is a saved prompt: a skill's instructions, filled in with what the writer typed, as their words. Read off the record, like `character`, so it still reads as one after its skill has gone. See `savedPrompt` in ai/commands.js.
- `load` **`true`?** With `prompt`: the skill is one the model could load too, so this loaded it for the rest of the chat — carried past a summary, listed as loaded, droppable. See ai/skills/loads.js.
- `dropped` **`true`?** A load the writer dropped: read where it is, and not carried past a summary. See ai/skills/loads.js.
- `label` **[string][111]?** The question, as the model reads it, when there was one. A direction the writer simply gave asked nothing.
- `detail` **[string][111]?** The working, for the writer only, when it is something that happened rather than something derivable. What to show is `commandDetail` — the oracle's odds are read back off `param`.
- `result` **[string][111]** What came back, empty while a consulting command is still asking
- `pending` **[boolean][113]?** Set while a command that costs a model call is running
- `reasoning` **[string][111]?** What it thought on the way to the answer, for the reader. Streamed in as it arrives.
- `thought` **[number][112]?** How long it thought, in milliseconds, measured to the first word of the answer
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why there is no result, when there is none
- `keep` **[number][112]?** Compaction only: how many turns the summary was put above when it was asked for, which it read all the same. The summary's place in the chat is what says what it stands for; this is how to ask it again over the same conversation, and how far to move it when the writer changes the count. See ai/compaction.js.

## DirectorNote

What the Director did before the assistant wrote, when the turn consulted it
rather than leaving the call to the model.

The reasoning is kept for the reader, not for the model: the Game Master is
handed `direction` and nothing else, because the whole point of a Director is
that its working stays out of the narration. Here it is the only way to see
why a direction came out the way it did.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `pending` **[boolean][113]?** Set while the call is in flight, cleared by the answer
- `reasoning` **[string][111]?** What the Director thought on its way to the direction
- `direction` **[string][111]?** What it told the Game Master
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why there is no direction, when there is none

## MessageAlternate

One of a message's answers.

A message asked again keeps what it said, and can be turned back to it.
Each answer is what one generation wrote to the message — its words, its
thinking, when it was written, and its record of what it did — and nothing
about where the message sits in its chat, which is the same for all of
them. The message's own fields are always the answer it is showing; see
`selectAlternate` in stores/messagesStore.js.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `content` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `reasoningContent` **([string][111] | null)?**&#x20;
- `streamingStartTime` **([number][112] | null)?**&#x20;
- `streamingFinishTime` **([number][112] | null)?**&#x20;
- `thinkingFinishTime` **([number][112] | null)?**&#x20;
- `thinkingTime` **([number][112] | null)?**&#x20;
- `edited` **[boolean][113]?**&#x20;
- `editedAt` **([number][112] | null)?**&#x20;
- `metadata` **([MessageMetadata][61] | null)?**&#x20;

## MessageSegment

One thing a turn was made of.

A submission is not always one thing: the writer rolls an oracle, says what
their character does, and tells the Director the scene has gone on long
enough. That is one turn — one speaker, taken in pieces — and the pieces are
these. See ai/commands.js.

Type: ({type: `"text"`, content: [string][111]} | {type: `"command"`, command: [ChatCommand][52]})

## DocumentEdit

A change a turn's tool made to a document, kept so the turn can be undone.

The pair is the smallest cut the two versions allow (see utils/edits.js):
undoing it finds `new` and puts `old` back, which survives the writer's own
edits elsewhere and refuses when they have edited the passage itself. A
creation carries what it created; undoing it removes the document, if the
document still says that.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Names the change, so a decision made on it while the turn is still writing survives the turn's next write
- `documentId` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `path` **[string][111]** Where the document was when it changed, for the writer
- `tool` **[string][111]** Which tool made the change
- `old` **[string][111]** The passage as it was; empty for an append or a creation
- `new` **[string][111]** The passage as the tool left it; the whole body for a creation
- `status` **(`"proposed"` | `"accepted"` | `"rejected"`)?** Set when the chat asks the writer first: proposed until they decide. Absent means the change went straight in. While proposed, `old` and `new` are the tool's own arguments, since they are what applies it; accepted, they become the pair that was applied.
- `summary` **[string][111]?** A proposed creation's summary, to give the document when it is created

## MessageMetadata

Message metadata structure.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `command` **[ChatCommand][52]?** The tool this message is a record of, when the writer ran one themselves rather than typing a message
- `director` **[DirectorNote][54]?** The Director's turn, when this chat runs it before the assistant
- `usage` **[TurnUsage][50]?** Token usage reported by the provider, when it reports any
- `model` **[string][111]?** Which model wrote this answer, as its provider names it. On the answer rather than the chat, because a chat changes presets as it goes and asking again on another one is half the reason to ask again. Absent on anything written before this was kept, and on a turn nobody generated.
- `provider` **[string][111]?** Where that model ran, by the name the writer gave the provider — the same model behind two of them is not the same thing. For a chat brought in from SillyTavern, the API it says it used.
- `documentEdits` **[Array][114]<[DocumentEdit][59]>?** What this assistant turn's tools changed in the project, in the order they changed it. Rewinding past the turn undoes them, newest first.
- `apiTrajectory` **[Array][114]<[ApiMessage][46]>?** The model's full per-iteration trajectory for this assistant turn (assistant deltas + tool calls + tool results + trailing assistant text). The record of what the turn called: the tool call panel shows it, and the context builder sends its calls back on every later turn without their text: every call when `callsKept`, the document calls when `documentCallsKept`, and its skill loads always. A past turn's words go back as its content. See ai/context/build.js.
- `callsKept` **`true`?** Every call this turn made goes back with the conversation. Set on every turn written since they began to; a turn from before keeps going back as it did. See ai/context/build.js.
- `documentCallsKept` **`true`?** This turn's document calls go back with the conversation. Set on turns written while only they did, before `callsKept`. See ai/context/reads.js.
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why the turn failed, when it did: the provider's own words, or the app's. Shown where the reply would have been, and gone when the message is asked again. Never sent to the model.

## PendingToolCall

A tool call the model is still writing, as far as it has got.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** The call's id, once the stream has said it
- `name` **[string][111]** Tool name
- `arguments` **[string][111]** The arguments JSON so far, likely cut off

## Message

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique message identifier (message_xxx)
- `chatId` **[string][111]** Parent chat ID
- `role` **(`"user"` | `"assistant"`)** Message sender role
- `content` **[string][111]** What the model is sent. For a message with segments this is assembled from them and never written by hand; see `assembleTurn`.
- `segments` **[Array][114]<[MessageSegment][58]>?** What the turn was made of, when it was made of more than prose. The writer's side only: a consultation is one speaker saying one thing and carries its record in `metadata.command` instead.
- `reasoningContent` **([string][111] | null)?** AI reasoning content (for assistant messages)
- `streamingStartTime` **([number][112] | null)?** Timestamp when streaming started
- `streamingFinishTime` **([number][112] | null)?** Timestamp when streaming finished
- `thinkingFinishTime` **([number][112] | null)?** Timestamp when thinking/reasoning finished
- `thinkingTime` **([number][112] | null)?** How long the turn spent thinking, in milliseconds, over every round it thought in. A turn that calls tools thinks again after each result, so this is the sum and not the time until thinking first stopped. Absent on turns from before it was kept, which read it as `thinkingFinishTime - streamingStartTime`.
- `pendingToolCalls` **[Array][114]<[PendingToolCall][63]>?** The calls the model is writing or the app is running right now, for the chat to show. In-flight only: cleared as each round's results land and when the turn ends.
- `alternates` **[Array][114]<[MessageAlternate][56]>?** Every answer the message has had, in the order they were asked for, the one it is showing among them. Only once it has been asked again; a message answered once has none.
- `alternate` **[number][112]?** Which of them it is showing.
- `edited` **[boolean][113]?** Whether the message has been edited
- `editedAt` **([number][112] | null)?** Timestamp when edited
- `metadata` **([MessageMetadata][61] | null)?** Additional message metadata
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## Lorebook

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique lorebook identifier (lorebook_xxx)
- `storyId` **[string][111]** Parent story ID
- `categories` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>** List of categories in this lorebook
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## ActivationKey

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `key` **[string][111]** Activation keyword
- `caseSensitive` **[boolean][113]** Whether the keyword is case sensitive
- `matchType` **(`"word"` | `"prefix"` | `"substring"`)** Match type

## LoreEntry

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique entry identifier (lore_xxx)
- `lorebookId` **[string][111]** Parent lorebook ID
- `name` **[string][111]** Entry name/title
- `category` **[string][111]** Entry category (characters, locations, items, concepts etc.)
- `description` **[string][111]** Short description of the entry
- `content` **[string][111]** Full entry content/description
- `activationKeys` **[Array][114]<[ActivationKey][69]>** Keywords that trigger this entry
- `enabled` **[boolean][113]** Whether entry is active
- `includeInPrompt` **[boolean][113]** Whether to include in AI prompts
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## Change

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `entityType` **[string][111]** Database table name
- `id` **[string][111]** Entity ID
- `op` **(`"put"` | `"delete"`)** Write the row, or remove it
- `data` **any** Changed data; null for a removal
- `timestamp` **[number][112]** Change timestamp

## StoreState

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `items` **[Map][116]<[string][111], any>** Map of items by ID
- `isInitialized` **[boolean][113]** Whether store is initialized
- `initializePromise` **([Promise][117] | null)** Initialization promise

## AIProvider

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique provider identifier (provider_xxx)
- `name` **[string][111]** User-friendly name for the provider
- `type` **(`"openrouter"` | `"anthropic"` | `"openai"` | `"gemini"` | `"llamacpp"` | `"generic"`)** Provider type. See ai/providers.js.
- `endpoint` **[string][111]?** API endpoint URL, for a type without a known address (see ai/providers.js)
- `apiKey` **[string][111]?** API key for authentication
- `rememberKey` **[boolean][113]?** Whether to persist API key in IndexedDB (default true). If false, key is stored in sessionStorage only
- `isDefault` **[boolean][113]?** Whether this is a default provider (cannot be deleted)
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## AIPreset

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique profile identifier (profile_xxx)
- `type` **[string][111]?** Profile type (legacy, retained for stored data compatibility)
- `name` **[string][111]** Profile name
- `providerId` **[string][111]** ID of the AI provider to use
- `model` **[string][111]** Model identifier
- `allowedProviders` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** OpenRouter only: the upstream providers allowed to serve this model, by slug. Absent or empty allows any the connection's routing does. Here rather than on the connection because it is a choice about the model. See ai/routing.js.
- `ignoredProviders` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** OpenRouter only: upstream providers never routed to for this model, by slug, on top of the connection's ignored ones. Absent or empty adds none.
- `toolsEnabled` **[boolean][113]?** Whether the model may call tools. Undefined is treated as enabled.
- `isDefault` **[boolean][113]** Whether this is a default profile
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution
- `created` **[number][112]** Creation timestamp
- `updated` **[number][112]** Last update timestamp

## StoredChatProfile

A chat profile the writer saved: how a chat is run, in one place.

The built-in profiles ship as source (`ai/profiles/index.js`); these are the
writer's own. `settings` is the same shape either way — see `ProfileSettings`
there — so nothing downstream has to know which kind it was handed.

The prompt library's rows became these and kept their ids, which is why some
of them are `prompt_xxx` rather than `chatprofile_xxx`. See
`stores/migrations/profiles.js`.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** chatprofile_xxx, or a migrated prompt_xxx
- `name` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `version` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `created` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `updated` **[number][112]**&#x20;

## SkillFile

One of the writer's own skills, as the library keeps it: the SKILL.md itself,
and the other files that came with it. The text is the skill; see
`ai/skills/format.js`.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** skill_xxx
- `name` **[string][111]** The name the text gives it, kept beside the text so
  the library can be looked up and kept unique without reading every file
- `text` **[string][111]** The SKILL.md
- `files` **[Array][114]<[SkillFile][83]>** The rest of its folder that is text
- `version` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `created` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `updated` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `path` **[string][111]** Where it sits in the skill's folder, e.g. `references/voice.md`
- `content` **[string][111]**&#x20;

## SkillWording

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `name` **[string][111]** The built-in skill it rewords
- `prompt` **[string][111]** What that skill runs under instead of its file's
  instructions, in every chat whose profile has no wording of its own
- `updated` **[number][112]**&#x20;

## WebServiceId

A search service the model can reach the web through. See web/services.js.

Type: (`"exa"` | `"kagi"` | `"brave"`)

## WebSearchSetup

How the writer set web search up, app-wide: one row, `id` 'web'.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **`"web"`**&#x20;
- `service` **[WebServiceId][87]?** The service in use. Absent means none is
- `keys` **Partial\<Record<[WebServiceId][87], [string][111]>>** The writer's key for
  each service they set one for, kept when they switch to another. Left out
  of backups unless the writer includes keys, as a provider's is: the
  services stay and the keys come back empty.
- `profiles` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>** The chat profiles whose chats search the
  web, unless a chat chooses otherwise
- `updated` **[number][112]?**&#x20;

## LibraryCard

A character card in the writer's library: what the grid, the search and the
hover need, and no more, so the whole library can be read when it opens.
The card itself is beside it, in a `CardFile` by the same id.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** libcard_xxx
- `name` **[string][111]** The character's, as the card gives it
- `title` **[string][111]** What the card is known by: its nickname, when it
  has one, and its name otherwise
- `creator` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `tags` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>**&#x20;
- `notes` **[string][111]** The creator's notes for people browsing, as plain
  text; the start of the description when there are none
- `greetings` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `lore` **[number][112]** How many entries its lorebook has
- `systemPrompt` **[boolean][113]** Whether it overrides the system prompt,
  which is the one thing asked when it goes into a project
- `hash` **[string][111]** A fingerprint of the card's JSON, which tells a
  card added twice
- `added` **[number][112]** When it came into the library
- `used` **[number][112]?** When it last went into a project
- `projects` **[Array][114]<[CardUse][92]>?** The projects it went into from the
  library, the newest last. One deleted since is left for whoever reads
  them to pass over.

## CardUse

A project a library card went into, and the folder it was written to there.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `storyId` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `folderId` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `made` **[boolean][113]?** The project was made for the card, by New project
- `at` **[number][112]** When

## CardFile

A library card's own data, read one at a time: the card as it arrived, the
PNG it came in, and a small copy of the picture for the grid.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** The library card's id
- `card` **any** The card's JSON, in whatever spec it was written to
- `image` **([Blob][115] | null)** The PNG it came in, whole; none for a JSON card
- `thumbnail` **([Blob][115] | null)?** Made from the image; a cache, left out of
  backups and made again when missing

## McpServer

An MCP server the writer has connected, app-wide like their skills.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** mcp_xxx
- `name` **[string][111]** What the writer calls it
- `prefix` **[string][111]** What its tools' names start with, made from the
  name when it was added and kept through renames. See mcp/names.js.
- `url` **[string][111]?** Where it answers
- `headers` **Record<[string][111], [string][111]>?** Sent with every request: an
  API key, usually. Left out of backups unless the writer includes keys, as
  a provider's key is: the names stay and the values come back empty, and
  an empty one is not sent.
- `auth` **`"oauth"`?** How the writer signs in to it, when they do. The
  sign-in itself is kept in this browser and never here; see mcp/auth.js.
- `command` **[string][111]?** For one that runs as a local program, which
  a page cannot start: kept so the writer can see it needs a bridge
- `args` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?**&#x20;
- `tools` **[Array][114]<[McpTool][98]>** Its tools as last listed
- `prompts` **[Array][114]<[McpPrompt][100]>** Its prompts as last listed
- `profiles` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>** The chat profiles whose chats use it, unless
  a chat chooses otherwise
- `allowed` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>** Its tools the writer always allows, by their
  own names, so a call to one runs without asking
- `allowAll` **[boolean][113]?** The writer always allows every tool it has,
  the ones it adds later included, so none of its calls asks
- `listedAt` **[number][112]?** When its tools were last listed
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why it could not be listed, the last time it was tried
- `created` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `updated` **[number][112]**&#x20;

## McpTool

A tool a server offers, as it described it.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `name` **[string][111]** The server's name for it
- `exposed` **[string][111]** The name the model calls it by. See mcp/names.js.
- `title` **[string][111]?**&#x20;
- `description` **[string][111]?**&#x20;
- `inputSchema` **[Object][110]** JSON Schema for its arguments

## McpPrompt

A prompt a server offers.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `name` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `title` **[string][111]?**&#x20;
- `description` **[string][111]?**&#x20;

## AIPrompt

A named system prompt the user has saved. App-wide rather than per-story, so
the same prompt can be loaded into any chat.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Unique prompt identifier (prompt_xxx)
- `name` **[string][111]** Display name, e.g. "Adventure" or "Editor"
- `content` **[string][111]** The prompt text
- `version` **[number][112]** Version number for conflict resolution

## JobStep

One step of a long job.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** Names the step within its job; a conversion's chunk id
- `label` **[string][111]** What the panel shows: `Pages 12–19`
- `status` **(`"pending"` | `"running"` | `"done"` | `"failed"`)**&#x20;
- `output` **[string][111]?** What the step produced, kept so the job resumes past it
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why it failed, when it did
- `tokens` **[number][112]?** What the step cost, when the provider said

## Job

A long job a model does for a project over many requests.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `id` **[string][111]** job_xxx
- `storyId` **[string][111]**&#x20;
- `kind` **[string][111]** Which kind of job; `convert`
- `workflow` **[string][111]** The workflow whose model runs it; see application state `workflows`
- `documentId` **[string][111]?** The document it works on, when it works on one
- `title` **[string][111]** What the panel calls it
- `status` **(`"queued"` | `"running"` | `"paused"` | `"done"` | `"failed"` | `"cancelled"`)**&#x20;
- `steps` **[Array][114]<[JobStep][104]>** In order; the runner takes the first not done
- `plan` **any?** What the kind planned from: a conversion's chunks and the text they index
- `error` **[string][111]?** Why the job failed, when it did
- `resultId` **[string][111]?** The document it wrote, once done: a conversion's copy
- `elapsed` **[number][112]?** How long it has run, in ms, over every run up to the last stop;
  the run in hand adds its own time from `jobs/live.js`
- `created` **[number][112]**&#x20;
- `updated` **[number][112]**&#x20;

## WorkflowSettings

Which model a workflow runs on: long work with needs of its own — a
conversion, later a summary — that may want a stronger or a cheaper model
than a chat does.

Type: [Object][110]

### Properties

- `providerId` **([string][111] | null)** The provider the workflow runs on; null for the active preset's
- `model` **([string][111] | null)** The model; null for the active preset's
- `allowedProviders` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** OpenRouter only: the upstreams allowed to serve the model, like a preset's. Read only when the workflow names its own provider; one that runs on the active preset runs on the preset's list.
- `ignoredProviders` **[Array][114]<[string][111]>?** OpenRouter only: the upstreams never routed to for the model, like a preset's, and read the same way as `allowedProviders`.
- `reasoningEffort` **([string][111] | null)?** How hard the model thinks: one of `REASONING_EFFORT_OPTIONS`, fitted to the model as it is sent;
  null for the app's default (`AI_DEFAULTS.reasoningEffort`)
- `onImport` **[boolean][113]?** Convert only: convert every file with text as it is imported
